title: Typing props: describe the object your component takes

slides.say: With TypeScript, your editor can tell you a prop is missing before you even run the app. It starts with typing props.
Props are one object, so you type that object. For a small component, write the type inline.
As it grows, move it to an interface or a type. A question mark makes a prop optional. Comments show up in your editor's hints.

slides.text: Use .tsx for files with JSX. Now <MyButton /> without title is flagged before you run anything.
slides.say: Remember: files with JSX need the dot T S X extension. Now, forgetting title gets flagged right in your editor.
